questions.question: What forms of long-term supply commitment do NVIDIA, AMD and Intel describe in their latest 10-K risk factors, and what happens to each if demand falls short?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says that to secure future supply and capacity it has paid premiums, provided deposits, and entered into long-term supply agreements and capacity commitments, which have increased its product costs [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. It also says it has entered into prepaid manufacturing and capacity agreements for current and future products [0001045810-26-000021:0023]. If demand falls short, NVIDIA says it may be unable to use on-hand inventory or reduce purchase commitments accordingly [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. It says it has had to reduce average selling prices, write down inventory, incur cancellation penalties and record impairments, and may have to do so again [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. It adds that non-cancellable and non-returnable purchase orders amplify these risks [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. It also says it may incur inventory provisions or impairments if its inventory or its supply or capacity commitments exceed demand [0001045810-26-000021:0023].
AMD says it has long-term purchase commitments and prepayment arrangements with some of its suppliers [0000002488-26-000018:0031]. If AMD overestimates demand or demand decreases, it says the result could be excess inventory and an increase in production costs, particularly because of its prepayment arrangements with certain suppliers [0000002488-26-000018:0031]. AMD is also party to a wafer supply agreement with GF, under which GF provides a minimum annual capacity allocation and sets pricing through 2026 [0000002488-26-000018:0030]. If AMD's actual wafer requirements are below the applicable annual wafer purchase target, it could have excess inventory or higher inventory unit costs, which may hurt its gross margin and results of operations [0000002488-26-000018:0030].
Intel says it has entered into arrangements with some suppliers that involve long-term purchase commitments and/or large prepayments, to obtain certain materials and components (particularly substrates) and third-party foundry manufacturing capacity [0000050863-26-000011:0075]. If future customer demand over the horizon of these arrangements falls below its expectations, Intel says it could have excess or obsolete inventory, unneeded capacity and increased costs [0000050863-26-000011:0075]. It adds that its prepayments may not be fully utilized, and in some cases may not be fully recoverable [0000050863-26-000011:0075].

It has also entered and may continue to enter into prepaid manufacturing and capacity agreements for current and future products [0001045810-26-000021:0023]. It continues to increase supply and capacity purchases with existing and new suppliers to support its demand projections and the growing complexity of its data center products [0001045810-26-000021:0023]. It is also increasing its U.S.-based manufacturing and investing in specialized equipment and processes for domestic production [0001045810-26-000021:0023]. In addition, it has expanded supplier relationships to build redundancy and resilience, and while its supply chain is mainly concentrated in Asia, it is expanding into the U.S. and Latin America [0001045810-26-000021:0012].
Risks from these commitments: NVIDIA says it may still be unable to secure sufficient capacity commitments for its business needs [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. If it inaccurately estimates demand or customers change orders, it may not be able to reduce supply commitments in time, at the same rate, or at all [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. It says significant supply and demand mismatches have resulted in both product shortages and excess inventory and have significantly harmed its financial results, and that they could recur [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. If it overestimates demand, it may be unable to use on-hand inventory or reduce purchase commitments, and it has had to write down inventory, incur cancellation penalties, and record impairments, and may have to do so again [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. These risks would be amplified by non-cancellable and non-returnable purchase orders placed in advance of historical lead times [0001045810-26-000021:0022]. NVIDIA also says the risks have increased and may continue to increase as purchase obligations and prepaids grow and become a greater portion of total supply, which may negatively affect gross margins and financial results [0001045810-26-000021:0022].

questions.question: How was Intel's sale of a majority stake in Altera structured, and how did it affect Intel's FY2025 financial statements?

answer.text:
Structure of the deal: On April 14, 2025, Intel signed a transaction agreement with SLP VII Gryphon Aggregator, L.P., an affiliate of Silver Lake Partners (SLP), to sell 51% of Altera's issued and outstanding common stock [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. Intel completed the divestiture on September 12, 2025, for net purchase consideration of $4.3 billion [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. The consideration consisted of $4.3 billion in cash proceeds at closing, $500 million in deferred cash proceeds also received in Q3 2025, and $500 million in deferred cash proceeds payable to Intel no later than December 31, 2027 [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. These amounts were offset by $400 million of cash transferred to Altera, about $469 million of separation and employee-related costs Intel agreed to fund to SLP, and other direct and incremental costs of the sale [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. Intel retained a 49% minority investment in Altera [0000050863-26-000011:0146]. Intel also provides wafer manufacturing services to Altera, a related party, under a wafer manufacturing and sale agreement, and is reimbursed for corporate services under a transition services agreement [0000050863-26-000011:0145].
Accounting and financial statement effects: Intel concluded that Altera is a VIE for which it is not the primary beneficiary, because the governance structure does not let Intel direct the activities that most significantly affect Altera's economic performance, so it deconsolidated Altera at the September 12, 2025 close [0000050863-26-000011:0146]. The retained interest is accounted for under the equity method and classified within equity investments [0000050863-26-000011:0146]. Its carrying value was $3.2 billion at December 27, 2025, and Intel's ownership interest was 48% [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. The investment was recognized as a non-cash investing activity in 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0146].
The sale produced a pre-tax gain of $5.6 billion in interest and other, net, which is net of costs Intel agreed to fund to SLP and of direct and incremental selling costs [0000050863-26-000011:0031]. The gain calculation was $4,266 million of proceeds net of cash sold and direct selling costs, $457 million of deferred consideration, $3,246 million fair value of the retained interest, less $1,962 million of net assets of Altera and $454 million of separation and employee-related costs and other, giving $5,553 million [0000050863-26-000011:0147]. About $2.1 billion of the gain came from remeasuring the retained Altera investment to fair value at the close date [0000050863-26-000011:0147].
Cash flow and balance sheet: Cash proceeds received in 2025 of $4.2 billion, net of cash sold and selling costs, are presented in net cash provided by investing activities [0000050863-26-000011:0147]. At December 27, 2025, Intel recorded $463 million in other long-term assets for the present value of deferred consideration from SLP [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. It also recorded $327 million in other accrued liabilities and $97 million in other long-term liabilities for separation and employee-related costs payable to SLP and not yet paid [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. Intel is still finalizing customary closing adjustments with SLP, which could change the final net cash proceeds and the gain on sale [0000050863-26-000011:0145].

questions.question: What did Intel's 2024 Restructuring Plan involve, and when did Intel expect it to be substantially completed, per the FY2024 10-K?

answer.text:
Intel's 2024 Restructuring Plan was a set of cost and capital reduction initiatives meant to adjust spending to current business trends while enabling its new operating model and continuing to fund investments in its core strategy of returning to product and process competitiveness [0000050863-25-000009:0021]. The initiatives include reducing headcount, consolidating and reducing the global real estate footprint, conducting portfolio reviews of its businesses under a "clean sheet" view, rationalizing capital investments and deployments based on demand signals and capacity requirements, and reducing overall operating expenses [0000050863-25-000009:0021]. The headcount actions were expected to result in an approximate 15% decrease in Intel's core workforce by early 2025 [0000050863-25-000009:0021][0000050863-25-000009:0016].
The plan was announced in Q3 2024, then approved and committed to by management, to implement cost-reduction measures including reductions in employee headcount, other operating expenditures, and capital expenditures [0000050863-25-000009:0039]. Its charges are primarily employee severance and benefit arrangements, non-cash asset impairments tied to exit activities, and charges for real estate exits and consolidations [0000050863-25-000009:0123]. Intel recognized restructuring charges of $2.8 billion in 2024 and expects total charges of approximately $3.0 billion under the plan [0000050863-25-000009:0021][0000050863-25-000009:0123].
Intel expected actions under the plan to be substantially completed by the fourth quarter of 2025, which is subject to change [0000050863-25-000009:0039][0000050863-25-000009:0123].

questions.question: What did Intel's FY2024 10-K say about its policy on dividends and stock repurchases, and what constrains its ability to return cash to stockholders?

answer.text:
Intel's capital allocation strategy historically included returning excess cash to stockholders through dividends and stock repurchases, but its most recent stock repurchase was in the first quarter of 2021 [0000050863-25-000009:0010]. Intel suspended the declaration of quarterly dividends starting with the fourth quarter of 2024 [0000050863-25-000009:0010][0000050863-25-000009:0043]. It does not expect to pay dividends or make stock repurchases until its cash flows improve, as it focuses on the critical investments needed to execute its business strategy and create long-term value [0000050863-25-000009:0010].
Intel agreed to forgo paying dividends for the next two years and agreed to limitations on dividend payments for the three years after that [0000050863-25-000009:0010][0000050863-25-000009:0073]. The MD&A states that Intel is prohibited under that agreement from paying dividends for the next two years and is subject to limitations for the three years thereafter [0000050863-25-000009:0043].
The risk factors add that there is no assurance Intel will be able to pay dividends in the future [0000050863-25-000009:0073]. Intel is also not obligated to make repurchases under its stock repurchase program, and there is no assurance about the amount, timing or execution of any future share repurchases, or that any repurchases will enhance long-term stockholder value [0000050863-25-000009:0073].
Intel's first allocation priority is investing in R&D and capital spending [0000050863-25-000009:0010]. In 2024 it invested $16.5 billion in R&D and made gross capital investments of $25.1 billion, with $8.3 billion in cash from operations and negative $2.2 billion of adjusted free cash flow [0000050863-25-000009:0020].

questions.question: According to Intel's FY2025 risk factors, what consequences would Intel face if it paused or discontinued development of Intel 14A and later leading-edge nodes?

answer.text:
Intel's FY2025 10-K says that if it paused or discontinued the design, development and manufacturing of Intel 14A and other next generation leading-edge nodes, it would face a number of significant strategic business, financial, operational and reputational risks and repercussions [0000050863-26-000011:0065].
Dependence on third-party foundries: Intel's products business would, over time, become dependent on third-party foundries, particularly TSMC, for nodes beyond Intel 18A and Intel 18A-P [0000050863-26-000011:0065]. Intel has no long-term contract with TSMC, and if it could not secure sufficient capacity on favorable pricing terms, it might be unable to manufacture its products in sufficient volume and at a cost that supports its products business [0000050863-26-000011:0065]. Most competitors have longer and more established relationships with TSMC and other third-party foundries, which may put Intel at a competitive disadvantage [0000050863-26-000011:0065]. Only TSMC and Samsung can currently produce the leading-edge and near-leading-edge nodes Intel's products need, so if competitors secured capacity more successfully, Intel's product roadmap, market position and customer relationships would be materially adversely impacted [0000050863-26-000011:0066].
Losses on R&D and manufacturing investments: Intel had over $100 billion of property, plant and equipment, net as of December 27, 2025, the substantial majority of which it estimates relates to its foundry business [0000050863-26-000011:0066]. Intel would expect significant material impairments of foundry assets, would likely discontinue the new leading-edge fabrication facilities it is building in Ohio, and would expect additional costs from winding down other projects and facilities and reducing headcount [0000050863-26-000011:0066].
Loss of government incentives: Intel may lose eligibility for various incentives under its government incentive arrangements and may be required to repay amounts already received [0000050863-26-000011:0066].
This could leave it unable to satisfy construction and/or wafer demand and purchase commitments in its arrangements with Brookfield (Arizona) and Apollo (Fab 34 in Ireland), potentially requiring substantial additional payments to its SCIP partners [0000050863-26-000011:0066].
A pause or discontinuation, or any perception that it may do so, may materially adversely impact its ability to hire and retain key talent across its foundry organization and the company more broadly, and it risks substantial loss of historical, technical and other expertise [0000050863-26-000011:0067].
Limited external foundry potential: Intel has been unsuccessful to date in attracting significant customers to its external foundry business, and if it paused or discontinued Intel 14A and successor nodes, it is highly uncertain whether it could develop this business [0000050863-26-000011:0067]. Potential customers for Intel 18A-P who believe Intel is no longer committed to next generation nodes may stay with their current foundry partners [0000050863-26-000011:0067].
These include adverse impacts on relationships and terms with customers, suppliers and strategic partners, potential credit rating risk, and diminished investor confidence and increased stock price volatility [0000050863-26-000011:0067]. It is also uncertain what actions the U.S. and other governments might take if they view a discontinuation as a strategic risk from a national economic or defense perspective [0000050863-26-000011:0067].
Intel says any of these could have a material adverse impact on its revenue, operations, financial position, cash flows, access to financing, cost structure, competitiveness, reputation, profitability and prospects [0000050863-26-000011:0067]. It adds that, given the decades of continuous investment required, any decision to pause or discontinue may be effectively irreversible [0000050863-26-000011:0067].

questions.question: What is the status of the third Texas patent case and the related license defense in Intel's VLSI litigation, according to the FY2025 10-K?

answer.text:
The third Texas case went to trial in November 2022 with VLSI asserting one remaining patent, and the jury found the patent valid and infringed and awarded VLSI approximately $949 million in damages, plus interest and a running royalty [0000050863-26-000011:0176]. The court has not yet entered final judgment [0000050863-26-000011:0176]. In February 2023, Intel filed motions for a new trial and for judgment as a matter of law notwithstanding the verdict, and further appeals are possible [0000050863-26-000011:0176].
On the license defense, Intel moved in April 2024 to add the defense that it is licensed to VLSI's patents, and the court granted the motion that same month [0000050863-26-000011:0176]. In May 2025, the court held a trial on an underlying factual question relating to the license defense, and the jury returned a verdict in Intel's favor [0000050863-26-000011:0176]. Post-trial briefing is complete, and the court will address the ultimate legal issue of whether Intel obtained a license to the asserted VLSI patent through its license agreement with Finjan when Fortress Investments acquired Finjan [0000050863-26-000011:0176].
The Delaware court has not taken further action and continues to receive status reports from the parties regarding the Texas court's consideration of Intel's license defense [0000050863-26-000011:0176].
As of December 27, 2025, Intel had accrued a charge of approximately $1.0 billion related to the VLSI litigation and was unable to make a reasonable estimate of losses in excess of recorded amounts [0000050863-26-000011:0177].

questions.question: How does NVIDIA's FY2026 10-K describe the oversight and management of cybersecurity risk?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says its information security management programs generally follow processes outlined in frameworks such as the ISO 27001 international standard, and that it consults external parties such as cybersecurity firms and risk management and governance experts [0001045810-26-000021:0054]. Cybersecurity risk identification, assessment and management is integrated into its overall risk management systems and processes, supported by cybersecurity and data privacy training and policies [0001045810-26-000021:0054]. It also runs a vendor risk assessment process that uses supplier questionnaires, and it routinely assesses its high-risk suppliers' conformance to industry standards such as ISO 27001, ISO 28001 and C-TPAT [0001045810-26-000021:0054].
On governance, the Board of Directors oversees information security matters, including managing and assessing risks from cybersecurity threats [0001045810-26-000021:0054]. The Audit Committee reviews the adequacy and effectiveness of the information security policies and practices and the related internal controls, and it receives regular updates from management, including the Chief Security Officer and members of the security team [0001045810-26-000021:0054]. The Board receives annual reports on information security matters from the Chief Security Officer and security team [0001045810-26-000021:0054].
Security efforts are managed by a team of executive cybersecurity, IT, engineering, operations and legal professionals, and a cross-functional executive leadership team meets regularly to review cybersecurity matters and evaluate emerging threats [0001045810-26-000021:0054]. That leadership team also takes part in incident response by engaging with the incident response team and helping direct the company's response to and assessment of certain incidents [0001045810-26-000021:0054]. NVIDIA has designated a Chief Security Officer, who reports to the Senior Vice President of Software Engineering and oversees the identification, assessment and management of material cybersecurity risks; the filing cites over 18 years of combined government and private sector assignments for this officer [0001045810-26-000021:0054].

questions.question: How did AMD's and Intel's gross margins move in fiscal 2025, and what drove the change at each company?

answer.text:
AMD's gross margin rose to 50% in fiscal 2025 from 49% in 2024 [0000002488-26-000018:0078]. Gross margin was 50% in Q1 2025 against 47% a year earlier, helped by higher Data Center revenue and a richer mix of Ryzen processor sales [0000002488-25-000047:0025]. Gross profit also benefited from reduced Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges relative to 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0043]. These favorable effects were partially offset by $878 million of higher 2025 inventory reserves, primarily lower of cost or net realizable value charges for products made on the early ramp of the Intel 18A process node [0000050863-26-000011:0043].
